chapters.title: Grow in virtue and heed the prophetic word

parts.text: Peter greets those sharing precious faith and explains that God’s power provides what is needed for life and godliness. His promises enable escape from worldly corruption and participation in the divine nature. Believers should diligently add virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and charity to faith. These qualities make them fruitful and confirm their calling and entrance into Christ’s everlasting kingdom.

Knowing his death is near, Peter intends to keep these truths before them. His witness to Christ’s majesty rests on what he saw and heard on the holy mount, not invented fables. The prophetic word deserves careful attention. Scripture’s prophecy is not of private interpretation: holy men spoke as the Holy Ghost moved them.

chapters.title: False teachers and their coming judgment

parts.text: Peter warns that false teachers will introduce destructive heresies, deny the Lord who bought them, and exploit people through covetous and deceptive words. Their judgment is certain. God’s dealings with sinful angels, the world of Noah, and Sodom and Gomorrha show that he knows both how to deliver the godly and how to reserve the unjust for punishment.

The teachers are described as presumptuous, lustful, greedy, and contemptuous of authority, following Balaam’s love of unrighteous gain. They promise freedom while themselves enslaved to corruption. Their empty boasts entice others back into evil. Returning to worldly pollution after knowing Christ leaves a person worse than before, like a washed sow returning to the mire.

chapters.title: The promised coming and the life it requires

parts.text: Peter recalls the words of prophets and apostles and warns of scoffers who deny the promised coming because things seem unchanged. They overlook God’s creation and the flood; the same word reserves the present world for fiery judgment. With the Lord, a day is as a thousand years and a thousand years as a day. His apparent delay is patience toward repentance, but the day will come unexpectedly and the present heavens and earth will be destroyed.

This prospect calls for holiness, godliness, and readiness for the promised new heavens and earth where righteousness dwells. Peter notes Paul’s agreement and warns against twisting difficult Scriptures. The readers must resist error and grow in Christ’s grace and knowledge.
